cells.tense: The thinking is already gathered and the hand is on the pen right now.
cells.ask: Before the next decision, write the two or three points that keep returning. Read the page once. Then act on it and let what happens be the information.
cells.core:
You can hold several threads at once and still pick one line forward. The thinking is gathered, and it comes out in what you decide and what you drop. When you end something now, it clears the way instead of making noise.

The fairness in this is quiet. You keep a clear sense of what's owed and what isn't, and you do it without recounting the ledger. People around you can feel that you're not keeping score even while you know where the line sits. The balance costs a bit of patience on the days when the right thing is slower than the fast thing. It holds anyway.

cells.tense: You are bracing for an ending that has not arrived yet.
cells.ask: Leave one thing you're already planning to end exactly where it is for a week. When it comes back to you, check whether you're still holding it or it's holding you. Act on the answer, not the plan.
cells.core:
Held well, this gathers without hurry. Threads come together at the pace the situation allows, you name the point once, and the ending arrives when it arrives. Nothing gets staged.

What happens instead is rehearsal. Each ending gets practiced before it's real, and the gathering turns into a case you're building. The push runs ahead of the actual ending, so the quiet part gets skipped. Your lines are ready and the saying keeps getting postponed one more round. What's underneath is simple movement — going when it's time to go. You can't schedule what isn't yours to schedule yet. Leave the thing where it sits and watch how the weight changes when you come back to it.

cells.tense: You walked past the door a long while ago and kept walking.
cells.ask: Pick the loosest thread — the one that costs you least to set down — and tell one person close to you that you're setting it down. No reasons needed. Let their hearing it be the whole act.
cells.core:
Done cleanly, the threads come up one at a time and get named. A quiet sentence to somebody who's close, and the knot loosens. The ending stops being a cliff and becomes a step, and you keep walking.

What you have instead is the old version still in your hands, carried without being carried anywhere. The gathering hasn't happened because the gathering needs somewhere to land, and the door is behind you. The quieter thing underneath strength is what's short here — knowing what the heart already settled on and letting that knowing hold still long enough to count. Pick the lightest thread and tell someone you're putting it down. The clearing starts from there.

cells.tense: The gathering is happening all on its own and you call it something else.
cells.ask: Name one decision you've been calling someone else's. Say out loud to one person: this one was mine. No explanation after it. Let them hear the sentence.
cells.core:
The threads are already gathered. You keep arriving at the same conclusion no matter where you start, and you describe it as though the conclusion were finding you. The clearing is underway. What's absent is your name on it.

When a group is in the room, you're the one shaping what gets remembered about the ending. That's transmission, and it belongs to you. The credit has been going to circumstance. Name one decision you've been calling someone else's, and say it was yours. The meaning gets shared out loud either way, so you might as well be in the room when it does.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is yours; you keep calling it circumstance.
